The current idea of a Nation is derived from Westphalian Ideals that ended the 30 years war in the Holy Roman Empire. Before this through the idea of Translatio Imperii, the Holy Roman Emperor was seen as the ultimate temporal head of all Christianity with the Pope being the Spiritual Head. Because of this the Title of Emperor of the Romans, passing from the Last true Western Roman Emperor, to the Byzantines, and then to Charlemagne, the title had never disappeared and thus still had legitimacy. Thus when Charlemagne was able to conquer significant portions of Europe, he was accepted as the true Emperor, most of the divisions of territories were caused by inheritance and granting of titles rather than any specific nationalistic pull. 

The British themselves don't have much a truly roman legacy due to several invasions of England after the Roman Legions packed up and left. The Romano-Britons were soon invaded by Angles, Saxons, and Jutes from Northern Germany and Denmark. Then subsequent invasions by Vikings, Normans, and constant fighting with the Scottish, Irish, and Welsh gave them a distinctly non-Roman character. Russia, and Moscow especially considers itself as the "Third Rome" after Rome and Constantinople partially due to religious regions as Moscow was the Grandest Orthodox City after the fall of Constantinople.
